disease_label_per_paper: Severe atypical bullous erysipelas induced by Escherichia coli in an immunosuppressed individual
presentation_summary: 60-year-old woman with 20-year rheumatoid arthritis on chronic methylprednisolone, leflunomide, and hydroxychloroquine presented with redness, swelling, heat, and pain in the left lower limb for one day, worsening with fever for four hours.

Four hours before presentation, temperature rose to 38.6 C and multiple blisters and blood blisters 2-3 cm in diameter appeared; some ruptured with light yellow exudate and subcutaneous hemorrhage, causing severe swelling and inability to walk.
Emergency lower-limb arterial/venous ultrasound showed no significant abnormality.
On admission, temperature was 36.6 C, pulse 128/min, respiratory rate 25/min, blood pressure 128/64 mmHg; she was conscious but agitated with moon face, buffalo hump, edema, and delicate skin.
Exam showed diffuse redness, swelling, heat, and pain from calf to dorsum of foot, with irregular vesicles and blood blisters, ulcerations, exudates, bleeding, and subcutaneous ecchymoses.
Labs showed CRP 334 mg/L, PCT >50 ng/mL, IL-6 >5500 pg/mL, WBC 8.4 x10^9/L, creatinine 189.5 umol/L, eGFR 24.3, lactate 6.3 mmol/L, bicarbonate 14.2 mmol/L, and low IgG/IgM/C3.
She progressed to septic shock with SOFA score 12 and multiple organ dysfunction, requiring ICU transfer, norepinephrine, non-invasive ventilation, CRRT, and liver protective measures.
Vesicle fluid culture and blood t-NGS confirmed Escherichia coli; after initial cefuroxime and broad escalation, therapy was de-escalated to piperacillin-tazobactam based on susceptibility.
After 10 days of intensive treatment, shock and organ injuries improved; after four months of multidisciplinary wound care, the wound healed completely.

quality_warnings: The confirmed E. coli organism is stored in microbiology with use_in_ranking=false, while presentation-rankable evidence preserves immunosuppression, bullous hemorrhagic morphology, shock physiology, inflammatory labs, and renal injury.
PCT and IL-6 were reported as greater-than values; lower-bound numeric values are encoded with quality notes.
The case is not renamed as Gram-negative erysipelas; Gram-negative context is represented as a pathogen/treatment-context axis.
